svg.font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

metadata.orrery:spec: # yaml-language-server: $schema=../references/diagram.schema.json title: VPC landing zone on IBM Cloud subtitle: Two VPCs across three zones joined by Transit Gateway, VPN to the data center, audit data in Object Storage direction: right # The tightest spacing keeps the five columns inside a README column at full label size. layout: { spacing: 0.5 } # IBM's technical diagram guide asks for a legend in every diagram, so solid lines get one too. legend: solid: Network traffic dashed: Key wrapping dotted: Flow logs and audit events # Follows the VPC landing zone deployable architecture (terraform-ibm-modules landing-zone): two # VPCs in one region, each with a server subnet and an endpoint subnet per zone, a VPN gateway in # the management VPC, a Transit Gateway between them and a flow log collector on each VPC. groups: # orrery has no IBM group styles; IBM's guide draws groups as plain outlined boxes, so these use # the neutral types with Carbon icons in the headers, as in ibm-cloud-openshift. The two VPCs sit # side by side with the Transit Gateway between them, as IBM's landing zone diagrams draw them. dc: { type: on-prem, label: On-premises } ibmcloud: { type: box, label: IBM Cloud, icon: ibm:ibm-cloud } region: { type: box, label: Region us-south, icon: ibm:location, in: ibmcloud } mgmt: { type: box, label: Management VPC, icon: ibm:virtual-private-cloud, in: region } m-z1: { type: dashed, label: Zone 1, icon: ibm:data-center, in: mgmt } m-z2: { type: dashed, label: Zone 2, icon: ibm:data-center, in: mgmt } m-z3: { type: dashed, label: Zone 3, icon: ibm:data-center, in: mgmt } work: { type: box, label: Workload VPC, icon: ibm:virtual-private-cloud, in: region } w-z1: { type: dashed, label: Zone 1, icon: ibm:data-center, in: work } w-z2: { type: dashed, label: Zone 2, icon: ibm:data-center, in: work } w-z3: { type: dashed, label: Zone 3, icon: ibm:data-center, in: work } # Two columns keep the services box within the management VPC's width. services: { type: box, label: Cloud services, in: region, cols: 2 } nodes: router: { icon: ibm:network-enterprise, label: Corporate router, note: VPN peer, in: dc } # The gateway sits in the one vpn subnet (zone 1) and routes to the servers in every zone. vpn: { icon: ibm:ibm-vpn-for-vpc, label: VPN for VPC, note: Site-to-site, in: mgmt } m1: { icon: ibm:ibm-cloud-virtual-server-vpc, label: Virtual servers, note: vsi-zone-1 subnet, in: m-z1 } m2: { icon: ibm:ibm-cloud-virtual-server-vpc, label: Virtual servers, note: vsi-zone-2 subnet, in: m-z2 } m3: { icon: ibm:ibm-cloud-virtual-server-vpc, label: Virtual servers, note: vsi-zone-3 subnet, in: m-z3 } tgw: { icon: ibm:ibm-cloud-transit-gateway, label: Transit Gateway, note: Local routing, in: region } w1: { icon: ibm:ibm-cloud-virtual-server-vpc, label: Virtual servers, note: vsi-zone-1 subnet, in: w-z1 } w2: { icon: ibm:ibm-cloud-virtual-server-vpc, label: Virtual servers, note: vsi-zone-2 subnet, in: w-z2 } w3: { icon: ibm:ibm-cloud-virtual-server-vpc, label: Virtual servers, note: vsi-zone-3 subnet, in: w-z3 } flow: { icon: ibm:flow-logs-vpc, label: Flow Logs for VPC, note: A collector on each VPC, in: services } cos: { icon: ibm:object-storage, label: Cloud Object Storage, note: Reached over VPE, in: services } atr: { icon: ibm:cloud-auditing, label: Activity Tracker Event Routing, note: Platform audit events, in: services } kp: { icon: ibm:ibm-cloud-key-protect, label: Key Protect, note: Root keys, in: services } edges: - router -> vpn: IPsec - vpn -> m1, m2, m3 # One Transit Gateway connection per VPC; the workload VPC has no VPN or public gateway of its own. - mgmt -> tgw - tgw -> w1, w2, w3 # Each VPC reaches Object Storage through a Virtual Private Endpoint in its vpe subnets (the note # on cos says so). constraint: false keeps the two lines from pulling the services box out from # under the VPCs. - mgmt -> cos: { constraint: false } - work -> cos: { constraint: false } - flow ..> cos - atr ..> cos # Buckets are encrypted with keys that Key Protect wraps (envelope encryption). - cos --> kp

svg.title: VPC landing zone on IBM Cloud
svg.desc: VPC landing zone on IBM Cloud. 13 components in 12 groups. Connections: Corporate router to VPN for VPC (IPsec); VPN for VPC to Virtual servers; VPN for VPC to Virtual servers; VPN for VPC to Virtual servers; Management VPC to Transit Gateway; Transit Gateway to Virtual servers; Transit Gateway to Virtual servers; Transit Gateway to Virtual servers; Management VPC to Cloud Object Storage; Workload VPC to Cloud Object Storage; Flow Logs for VPC to Cloud Object Storage; Activity Tracker Event Routing to Cloud Object Storage; Cloud Object Storage to Key Protect.

text.tspan: VPC LANDING ZONE ON IBM CLOUD
Two VPCs across three zones joined by Transit Gateway, VPN to the data center, audit data in Object Storage
